free_tier.stated: Quota is set by each game's developer as 'Byte quota per user' and 'Number of files allowed per user', 'enforced on each Cloud-enabled game, on a per-user-per-game basis'. No Valve-imposed total. Community-observed ceilings: 93 GB per game, ~10,000 files. Defaults are frequently tiny (a few MB to 1 GB).

retention.stated: Per-object-cap: 100 MB per FileWrite call (256 MB 'may result in a non-optimal storage endpoint'); per-object-cap: ~10,000 files per cloud save; the game must be launchable/owned for the user, and impersonating it blocks normal play during sync. Retention: indefinite. No expiry documented, but a developer can change quota or delist and the data can be evicted.

egress.terms: Unmetered and anonymous on the download path via the Steam client / Steamworks SDK. No published per-GB charge.

record.tooling: Steamworks SDK `ISteamRemoteStorage` (FileWrite, FileWriteStreamWriteChunk, FileReadAsync). Working wrapper exists: github.com/Fldicoahkiin/SteamCloudFileManager. 237 stars, Rust, Windows/macOS/Linux, '支持任意文件的上传、下载与删除' (arbitrary file upload/download/delete against any owned game's cloud). Design writeup: krutonium.ca/posts/using-steam-as-cloud-storage/.
record.chaining: One Steam account x every owned Cloud-enabled game with a large quota. At 93 GB/game, 12 games = ~1.1 TB; 100 games = ~9 TB. Multiply again by accounts. The lever is picking titles whose developers set 93 GB, not buying storage.
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap: 100 MB per FileWrite call (256 MB 'may result in a non-optimal storage endpoint'); per-object-cap: ~10,000 files per cloud save; the game must be launchable/owned for the user, and impersonating it blocks normal play during sync. Retention: indefinite. No expiry documented, but a developer can change quota or delist and the data can be evicted.
record.reliability_note: Entirely undocumented by Valve; a developer lowering their quota can strand data, and files are re-downloaded into the local save folder on game launch. No public bans recorded.

free_tier.stated: Per-item size is set by the game developer, not by Valve, and some games are explicitly unlimited. Arma 3: 'Arma 3 Workshop now support items of unlimited size.' Others are tiny: House Flipper raised its cap from 12 MB to 20 MB in a patch. So the quota is per-app, and the number of published items per account is not documented as capped.

egress.terms: Free and CDN-served by Valve's content network. Same infrastructure as game downloads, genuinely unmetered.

record.tooling: `ISteamUGC` (CreateItem + SetItemContent + SubmitItemUpdate) via the Steamworks SDK, so uploads need a Steam client with the game installed. Downloads are scriptable anonymously: `steamcmd +login anonymous +workshop_download_item <appid> <publishedfileid>`. Third-party downloaders (polocaz/ws-downloader, workshopfetch.com) exist for the read path.
record.chaining: One Steam account x every Workshop-enabled game it owns x unlimited items per game. This is the multiplier: 'unlimited items per published file ID' inside an app whose developer set no cap.

limits.value: review images go through a separate Steam Cloud quota

record.limits_note: Requires ownership of the game and a Steam client to upload. There is no headless upload path, which is the practical blocker. Per-item caps range from 20 MB to unlimited depending on app; preview images go through a separate Steam Cloud quota.
record.reliability_note: Very durable. Workshop items have survived a decade, links do not expire, and downloads are anonymous. Enforcement risk is real but technical: items can be delisted by the app's developer.

evidence.proved: 'What is the maximum size of a mod? Arma 3 Workshop now support items of unlimited size.'
'Increased the maximum Steam Workshop item size limit from 12 MB to 20 MB. Increased the default Workshop item size from 10 MB to 12 MB.'
'The maximum size varies depending on what the developers set it as.'
'Steam Workshop is a system of back-end storage and front-end web pages that make it easy to store, organize, sort, rate, and download content'

record.notes: Per-item size is set by the game developer, not by Valve, and some games are explicitly unlimited. Arma 3: 'Arma 3 Workshop now support items of unlimited size.' Others are tiny: House Flipper raised its cap from 12 MB to 20 MB in a patch. So the quota is per-app, and the number of published items per account is not documented as capped.
